newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealanders eating more beef - Meat Board.
newsitem.headline: New Zealanders eating more beef - Meat Board.

text.p: New Zealanders ate 10.5 percent more beef in the year to September 1996, the Meat Board said on Monday.
Average beef consumption was 38 kg per person out of a total red meat intake of 58.8 kg, compared with an average 24 kg of chicken.
Meat Board Chairman John Acland said price movements were the main driver of consumption trends. Domestic lamb consumption had fallen as the price was pushed up by higher prices overseas.

"At the same time beef prices have eased, largely driven by the increased volume of beef produced in the United States. These lower prices have encouraged New Zealanders to substitute beef for lamb," Acland said.
Television advertising stressing the importance of iron in people's diet was another probable factor behind the rise in beef consumption. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
